title: Theorem on formal functions at a point of the base
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism] with $Y$ locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent] and let $y\in Y$, with local ring $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ (a Noetherian local ring) and maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_y$. For $n\ge1$ let $c_n:\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O_{Y,y}/\mathfrak m_y^n)\to Y$ be the canonical morphism (induced by $\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to\mathcal O_{Y,y}/\mathfrak m_y^n$), $X_n=\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O_{Y,y}/\mathfrak m_y^n)\times_YX$ the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] (the $n$th infinitesimal neighbourhood of the fibre $X_1=X_y$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]), $i_n:X_n\to X$ the projection and $\mathcal F_n=i_n^*\mathcal F$ [def-pc-module-pullback]; the closed immersions $j_n:X_n\to X_{n+1}$ (base change of $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O_{Y,y}/\mathfrak m_y^n)\to\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O_{Y,y}/\mathfrak m_y^{n+1})$, with $i_{n+1}\circ j_n=i_n$) induce maps $H^p(X_{n+1},\mathcal F_{n+1})\to H^p(X_n,\mathcal F_n)$ [pqf-def-cohomology] (pullback along $j_n$ [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] followed by the canonical isomorphism $j_n^*\mathcal F_{n+1}\cong\mathcal F_n$), each $H^p(X_n,\mathcal F_n)$ being an $\mathcal O_{Y,y}/\mathfrak m_y^n$-module. Fix $p\ge0$ and let $M=(R^pf_*\mathcal F)_y$ be the stalk at $y$ of the higher direct image [pqf-def-cohomology], an $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$-module, and $M^\wedge=\varprojlim_nM/\mathfrak m_y^nM$ its $\mathfrak m_y$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Since $R^pf_*\mathcal F$ is the sheaf associated with $V\mapsto H^p(f^{-1}(V),\mathcal F)$ [lem-weil-pbc-higher-direct-image-presheaf], $M=\varinjlim_{V\ni y}H^p(f^{-1}(V),\mathcal F)$; as $X_n\to X$ factors through $f^{-1}(V)$ for every open $V\ni y$, pulling back along $X_n\to f^{-1}(V)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] defines $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$-linear maps $\theta_n:M\to H^p(X_n,\mathcal F_n)$, compatible with the transition maps and vanishing on $\mathfrak m_y^nM$. Then the induced map $\theta:M^\wedge\to\varprojlim_nH^p(X_n,\mathcal F_n)$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$-modules (indeed of $\mathcal O_{Y,y}^\wedge$-modules), and its composite with $M\to M^\wedge$ is $(\theta_n)_n$. In particular ($p=0$, $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$, so $\mathcal F_n=\mathcal O_{X_n}$) $(f_*\mathcal O_X)_y^\wedge\cong\varprojlim_nH^0(X_n,\mathcal O_{X_n})$ via the maps $(f_*\mathcal O_X)_y\to H^0(X_n,\mathcal O_{X_n})$ sending the germ of $t\in\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}(V))$ to its pullback to $X_n$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma Tag 02OD (lemma-formal-functions-stalk, line 5721) and its proof (flat base change to Spec O_{Y,y}, Lemma 02KH lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, then Theorem 02OC theorem-formal-functions); the description of the maps theta_n is the one in the proof of Tag 0G7X (perfect.tex, lines 8130-8157), which uses that M^ -> H^0(X_1) is the canonical map

proof.text: Apply the uncompleted local dictionary. It supplies coherence of the actual pullback module F′, the stalk/cohomology equivalence a, the natural isomorphism b of finite quotient systems over A, and canonical stalk maps theta whose values agree with quotient restriction after a and b. This is exactly the geometric portion of the original route, without the completion assertion.

Apply theorem_formal_functions over the Noetherian stalk ring A to the proper base-changed map, the extended maximal ideal J and F′. Complete a, restrict its completed-linear equivalence to A, compose with the theorem’s isomorphism and the limit of b, and use preservesLimitIso for restriction of scalars. This gives an A-linear equivalence v from the completion of M to the underlying A-module of the completed-linear fibre limit. Its nth projection is computed using preservesLimitIso_inv_π, isoOfNatIso_hom_π, the formal-functions projection formula, and map_val_apply for completion. The quotient-factorization formula and the dictionary identify it with theta_n(z) whenever eval_(n+1)(x)=z mod m^(n+1).

Transition compatibility follows by evaluating limit.w on v(of(z)). If z belongs to m^(n+1)M, its quotient class is zero; apply the projection formula with representatives z and 0 to obtain theta_n(z)=0. The same formula on of(z) proves the claimed composite with the completion map.

Prove completed-ring linearity in the private helper completion_map_linear. Represent a completed scalar and completed vector by adic Cauchy sequences. At level n+1 their product is represented by the product of their nth representatives. The projection formula and A-linearity of theta therefore identify the projected image of r*x with that of r*v(x); the fibre scalar action is through eval_(n+1), giving precisely the same scalar representative. Concrete.limit_ext identifies the two elements. Upgrade the underlying additive equivalence of v to an A-completion-linear equivalence using this proved scalar identity, retaining both projection formulas.

Degree-zero specialization (implemented in Lean; steps 1--9 remain the plan for the still-open general theorem). Properness makes X locally Noetherian, so the unit module is coherent by the coherence criterion and its finite locally free presentation. Apply the general formal_functions_stalk at p=0 to O_X. The degree-zero dictionary gives a on stalks and b on systems, with the germ formula. Complete a using AdicCompletion.congr, and apply HasLimit.isoOfNatIso to b. Compose these two isomorphisms with the general formal-functions isomorphism. AdicCompletion.map_of commutes the first factor with the canonical map to completion. HasLimit.isoOfNatIso_hom_π commutes the last factor with every projection. The general component formula followed by the dictionary germ formula is the desired section pullback.
